title: Proposal for graceful degradation curves and staged rollback conditions
creator: Marco Rivera
description: Summary: Create a prescriptive PRD and acceptance criteria that define tiered graceful-degradation curves, error-budget saturation behavior, and staged rollback conditions for multi-tenant hosted inference routes. Motivation: Teams have differing latency sensitivity and error tolerances; current rollout gates are binary and cause either immediate rollback or silent degradation. This ticket scopes a medium-term solution: (1) establish workload classes (interactive, background, batch) with explicit latency bands and acceptable partial-degradation modes; (2) define error-budget accounting and burn-rate thresholds tied to automated gates; (3) specify staged rollback and throttling actions (soft-throttle, model-variant fallback, regional shift, full rollback) with clear sequencing and escalation; (4) update Console runbooks and runtime indicators to reflect degradation state. Benefits: less noisy rollbacks, predictable customer experience during capacity or model regressions, reduced unnecessary full rollbacks, clearer on-call playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Three workload classes (interactive, background, batch) with numeric 50/95/99 latency bands documented for small/medium/large request sizes
Error-budget accounting formula documented and examples for tenant-level, project-level, and global budgets

Automated rollout gate rules: low/medium/high burn-rate thresholds that trigger (a) telemetry annotation and customer-affecting alert, (b) soft-throttle at percentage levels, (c) model-variant fallback, (d) staged regional shift, (e) full rollback - with conditions for each step
Console widgets and a /rollout/debug endpoint show degradation state and error-budget remaining per route
Runbook and escalation checklist authored, reviewed by SRE and Support, stored in Confluence link provided
Canary test plan and acceptance tests (synthetic traffic shapes) added to the automation repo with green checks before gating rollout
